question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined part in the given sentence:

Sohan was __very much perplexed__ to find that his younger brother Mohan had taken poison.
solution:
The correct answer is ***Option 2)***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"At his wit’s end"** means being so perplexed or confused that one does not know what to do. (हक्का-बक्का होना)

 
 
• **Example: **After trying everything to fix the computer, he was* **at his wit's end.***
 
 
 
• **"Perplexed"** refers to being completely baffled or puzzled. (हैरान)
 
 
• **Example: **She was ***perplexed ***by the sudden change in his behavior.
 
 

Therefore, the correct idiom is '***At his wit’s end'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **At any rate** (किसी भी हालत में): Regardless of the circumstances.

 
 
• **Example:** ***At any rate***, we must finish this project by tomorrow.
 
 
 
• **At loggerheads** (झगड़ालू होना): In strong disagreement.
 
 
• **Example: **The two colleagues were ***at loggerheads*** over the new policy.
 
 
 
• **At his disposal** (उसके पास उपलब्ध): Available for someone to use.
 
 
• **Example:** He has a car ***at his disposal ***for the weekend.
 
 

39:Td02,

The correct answer is ***Option 2)***
